Agent Name: GameTheory_Expert  
Step Number: 1  
Reason for Mistake: The first error is in the game-theory reasoning. The agent incorrectly treats the coin counts as if Bob can choose guesses that “cover all possible configurations” and thereby guarantee winning all 30 coins. That is not valid: Bob must submit one fixed set of three guesses before the boxes are revealed, and his payout depends on the actual hidden distribution. The listed distributions are also not derived correctly; the condition “one box contains 6 more coins than another” does not imply the specific tuples given, and the conclusion that guessing \(2,11,17\) guarantees 30 coins is false. The optimal strategy requires analyzing the worst-case guaranteed payoff across all valid distributions, not simply picking the minimum possible counts from one arrangement.
